description: Two-panel composite of cyclic voltammetry (CV) curves for low-density steels S950, S1050 and S1150 in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. Both panels share axes: Applied potential (V_SCE), -1.2 to -0.2, versus Current density (µA/cm²), -400 to 200. (a) first cycle: three curves (S950 green, S1050 blue, S1150 magenta) rise steeply at potentials more negative than about -1.05 V_SCE and show a broad anodic hump; a dashed box labelled "Al" with a red dashed vertical line marks the Al oxidation region, and an inset (Applied potential -1.0 to -0.6 V_SCE, Current density 0-120 µA/cm²) magnifies it with a red downward arrow at a single peak near -0.81 V_SCE, where the S950 curve is highest and S1050/S1150 lie close together below it. (b) second cycle: the dashed box is wider and labelled both "Al" and "Fe/Mn" with two red dashed vertical lines, and the inset (-0.9 to -0.4 V_SCE, 0-120 µA/cm²) resolves two peaks marked by two red arrows; S950 shows the lowest Fe/Mn peak while S1050 and S1150 are much stronger. No numeric values are printed on the curves. Together the panels argue that an Al-rich surface film on S950 forms in the first cycle and suppresses subsequent Fe/Mn oxidation.

observations.observation: Both panels plot Current density (µA/cm²) from -400 to 200 on the y-axis against Applied potential (V_SCE) from -1.2 to -0.2 on the x-axis.
The legend lists three samples, S950 (green), S1050 (blue) and S1150 (magenta), present in both panel (a) and panel (b).
Panel (a) contains a dashed box labelled 'Al' with a red dashed vertical line and an inset that magnifies the Al oxidation region, where a red downward arrow points to a single current peak.

In the panel (a) inset (potential -1.0 to -0.6 V_SCE, current density 0-120 µA/cm²) the green S950 curve attains the highest peak, near the -0.8 V gridline, while the blue S1050 and magenta S1150 curves are lower and close together.

Panel (b) contains a wider dashed box labelled both 'Al' and 'Fe/Mn' with two red dashed vertical lines, and its inset (-0.9 to -0.4 V_SCE, 0-120 µA/cm²) shows two peaks marked by two red downward arrows.
In the panel (b) inset at the Fe/Mn peak, the green S950 curve is the lowest of the three while the S1050 and S1150 curves show substantially larger peak current densities.
Panel (a) is the first cycle and panel (b) is the second cycle of the cyclic voltammetry measurement in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
The Al oxidation peak is assigned at approximately -0.81 V_SCE and the Fe oxidation peak at approximately -0.56 V_SCE, possibly with concurrent minor Mn oxidation.
In the first cycle the S950 sample exhibits the highest Al oxidation peak current density, indicating superior surface Al oxidation activity.
The Al oxidation peak region charge density in the first cycle is reported as 2.55×10⁻⁵ C/cm² for S950, 1.80×10⁻⁵ C/cm² for S1050 and 1.66×10⁻⁵ C/cm² for S1150.
The characteristic Fe oxidation peak near -0.56 V_SCE is absent in the first cycle, confirmed by repeated experiments (Supporting Information Fig. S1).
In the second cycle a distinct Fe oxidation peak emerges near -0.56 V_SCE and the S950 sample displays the lowest peak intensity there, whereas S1050 and S1150 show enhanced anodic peaks.
XPS results cited as confirmation show the S950 oxide film has higher Al content and reduced Fe and Mn concentrations than the other samples.

subfigures.description: First-cycle cyclic voltammetry curves of S950 (green), S1050 (blue) and S1150 (magenta) in 3.5 wt% NaCl; x-axis Applied potential (V_SCE) -1.2 to -0.2, y-axis Current density (µA/cm²) -400 to 200. A dashed box labelled 'Al' and a red dashed line mark the Al oxidation region; the inset (potential -1.0 to -0.6 V_SCE, current density 0-120 µA/cm²) zooms this region with a red arrow at a peak near -0.81 V_SCE, S950 being the highest curve.

Second-cycle CV curves of the same three samples. The dashed box is wider and labelled both 'Al' and 'Fe/Mn' with two red dashed vertical lines; the inset (-0.9 to -0.4 V_SCE, 0-120 µA/cm²) shows two peaks marked by two red downward arrows, with the S950 curve lowest at the Fe/Mn peak and S1050/S1150 markedly higher.
